### Headline summary
- French bank Crédit Mutuel Arkéa lost up to $133 million after attackers exploited a third-party service provider. ([Security Affairs](https://securityaffairs.com/202628/cyber-crime/attackers-exploit-third-party-provider-to-raid-french-bank-credit-mutuel-arkea.html))
- Japanese manufacturer Iris Ohyama disclosed that personal data of 7.7 million customers was exposed following unauthorized access to a third-party cloud. ([BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/iris-ohyama-data-cloud-breach-exposes-info-of-77-million-customers/))
- Honeypots report a surge in exploitation attempts for the Sshole vulnerability, while Microsoft disclosed two flaws in the Windows Cloud Files driver. ([SANS Internet Storm Center](https://isc.sans.edu/diary/rss/33498), [Talos](https://talosintelligence.com/vulnerability_reports/TALOS-2026-2426), [Talos](https://talosintelligence.com/vulnerability_reports/TALOS-2026-2445))

### Attackers Exploit Third-Party Provider to Raid French Bank Crédit Mutuel Arkéa
French Bank Crédit Mutuel Arkéa says hackers exploited a service provider to steal up to $133 million using the bank’s own account. French cooperative bank Crédit Mutuel Arkéa was hit by a cyberattack that let attackers make fraudulent transactions of up to $133 million, forcing it to suspend certa… ([Security Affairs](https://securityaffairs.com/202628/cyber-crime/attackers-exploit-third-party-provider-to-raid-french-bank-credit-mutuel-arkea.html))

### Iris Ohyama data cloud breach exposes info of 7.7 million customers
Japanese manufacturer Iris Ohyama, the operator of the Iris Plaza shopping platform, disclosed that personal information belonging to about 7.7 million people may have been exposed after unauthorized access to a third-party cloud service the company used. ([BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/iris-ohyama-data-cloud-breach-exposes-info-of-77-million-customers/))

### Scans for Sshole Vulnerability (CVE-2026-123158), (Sun, Nov 8th)
Our honeypots use "Cowrie" to collect SSH data. With the emergence of the "sshole" vulnerability last week, we are now seeing an increase in attempts to exploit the vulnerability. ([SANS Internet Storm Center](https://isc.sans.edu/diary/rss/33498))

### Microsoft Windows Cloud Files driver vulnerabilities
Microsoft disclosed two vulnerabilities in the Windows Cloud Files Mini Filter Driver, including a use-after-free and a type confusion flaw. ([Talos](https://talosintelligence.com/vulnerability_reports/TALOS-2026-2426), [Talos](https://talosintelligence.com/vulnerability_reports/TALOS-2026-2445))

### Fake Google Meet Updates, Abused RMM Tools, the AgtaBackup RAT Ecosystem & Campaign
How a fraudulent video-conferencing update can turn legitimate remote administration software into an attacker-controlled foothold, potentially enabling a second-stage remote access Trojan Introduction A user attempts to access what appears to be a legitimate Google Meet session. Instead of joining… ([Detect.fyi](https://detect.fyi/fake-google-meet-updates-abused-rmm-tools-the-agtabackup-rat-ecosystem-campaign-814b6f09541c?source=rss----d5fd8f494f6a---4))

### Claude Code “Don’t Ask Again” Approvals Exposed 2,539 Secrets on GitHub
When you tell Claude Code “Yes, and don’t ask again,” it saves the approved command word for word, password included. Researchers found more than a thousand of those files on public GitHub with secrets inside. ([Privacy Affairs](https://www.privacyaffairs.com/claude-code-dont-ask-again-secrets/))

### An Expired Domain Left South Korea’s Cyber Security Agency Open to DNS Hijacking
For an unknown stretch of time, anyone could have registered a domain that ran part of the DNS of South Korea’s National Cyber Security Center. That is the agency where people report security holes in government systems. ([Privacy Affairs](https://www.privacyaffairs.com/south-korea-ncsc-dns-hijacking/))

### DataSuckers : trois suspects arrêtés après une fuite
Trois suspects liés à DataSuckers arrêtés après le piratage de Dodo Pizza et le vol de millions de données. ([ZATAZ](https://www.zataz.com/datasuckers-trois-suspects-arretes-apres-une-fuite/))
